content:
Apple has recently raised prices on most of its products, but more increases are expected next month, covering iPhone and other products.

With the launch of the iPhone 18 series, iPhone prices are expected to rise, and Apple Watch and AirPods may also be affected.

Earlier this summer, Apple raised prices on many of its products.

Mac, iPad, Apple TV, HomePod, and Vision Pro all saw price hikes at the same time.

CEO Tim Cook had previously hinted that price increases were coming, but the breadth of the hikes across so many products is still shocking.

In the first wave of price increases, the only flagship products that were unaffected were:

  • iPhone
  • Apple Watch
  • AirPods

At the time, Apple hinted that more price increases would come in the future, and analysts believe the few products that initially escaped the price hikes will soon face the same fate.

There is now widespread expectation that Apple will raise iPhone prices at its September iPhone 18 launch event.

According to rumors, the iPhone 18 Pro will start at between $1,299 and $1,399, up from the iPhone 17 Pro's $1,099.

Apple typically cuts prices on older iPhone models when new ones launch, but this year older models are expected to stay at their current prices or see only modest increases.

The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are also likely targets for price hikes, as the current AI-driven memory crisis will affect watch components.

Finally, AirPods could also see price increases. Though AirPods should be less affected by rising memory and storage chip costs, price hikes are less likely than for iPhone and Apple Watch.

However, if Apple plans to raise prices across its entire product lineup, including AirPods, the September launch event will be when we find out.

What price adjustments do you expect from Apple? Let us know in the comments.
